ports.name: i_a_size
ports.meaning: TL-UL a_size (log2 of the number of bytes)

ports.name: i_a_address
ports.meaning: TL-UL a_address (byte address; the register offsets of the gpio specification are relative to 0)

ports.name: i_a_instr
ports.meaning: 1: the request is an instruction fetch (a_user.instr_type = MuBi4True); 0: a data access (MuBi4False)

ports.name: i_a_intg_flip
ports.meaning: 1: the A-channel integrity sent with the request is corrupted (see 4.2)

ports.name: o_d_intg_err
ports.meaning: Response integrity of the D-channel beat is wrong (see 4.3)

ports.name: o_alert_integ_fail
ports.meaning: Signal integrity failure on the alert differential pairs (see 5)

ports.name: o_gpio
ports.meaning: GPIO outputs cio_gpio_o: the value of DATA_OUT (see 6)

ports.name: o_gpio_en
ports.meaning: GPIO output enables cio_gpio_en_o: the value of DATA_OE (see 6)

checks.title: Alert signal integrity never fails
checks.behavior: At every rising edge of clk_i with rst_ni=1, o_alert_integ_fail=0. This includes the time while the alert is firing after a write to ALERT_TEST or after an integrity error.

checks.title: o_alert is a single-cycle pulse
checks.behavior: If o_alert=1 at rising edge N with rst_ni=1, then o_alert=0 at rising edge N+1.

checks.title: No alert without an alert cause
checks.behavior:
o_alert may be 1 at rising edge N (rst_ni=1) only if one of these holds since the last reset release:
(a) an A handshake with i_a_intg_flip=1 took place at an edge at or before N, or
(b) an A handshake of a write (a_opcode 0 or 1) to 0xC (ALERT_TEST) with i_a_data[0]=1 took place, and its D handshake is still pending or happened at edge N-16 or later.
So traffic with i_a_intg_flip=0 (correct integrity added by the wrapper) never raises an alert.

checks.title: o_gpio / o_gpio_en follow the DATA_OUT / DATA_OE shadow model
checks.behavior:
Shadow model: shadow_out and shadow_oe start at 32'h0 while rst_ni=0. At the D handshake of a write (a_opcode 0 or 1) with o_d_error=0, the shadow is updated from the stored address and data:
- 0x14 DIRECT_OUT: shadow_out=data.
- 0x18 MASKED_OUT_LOWER: for i in 0..15, if data[16+i]=1 then shadow_out[i]=data[i].
- 0x1C MASKED_OUT_UPPER: for i in 0..15, if data[16+i]=1 then shadow_out[16+i]=data[i].
- 0x100+4*i PER_PIN_IO_i: shadow_out[i]=data[0].
- 0x20 DIRECT_OE: shadow_oe=data.
- 0x24 MASKED_OE_LOWER and 0x28 MASKED_OE_UPPER: same rule as MASKED_OUT_* applied to shadow_oe.
- 0x200+8*i PER_PIN_OE_i: shadow_oe[i]=data[0].
Let Ed be the D handshake edge of the last such write. At every rising edge from Ed+2 until the next A handshake of a write to one of these addresses: o_gpio==shadow_out and o_gpio_en==shadow_oe. Also from reset release until the first write: o_gpio=0 and o_gpio_en=0. The check is disabled from an A handshake with i_a_intg_flip=1 until rst_ni=0.

checks.title: D-channel response integrity never fails
checks.behavior: At every rising edge of clk_i with rst_ni=1, o_d_intg_err=0, whether o_d_valid is 0 or 1. The check stays on after a request with i_a_intg_flip=1, because D-017 requires it in every cycle with rst_ni=1. Runs in all four configurations.

checks.title: Disabled interrupts never assert o_intr_gpio
checks.behavior: Shadow model: shadow_en=0 while rst_ni=0. At the D handshake (edge Ed) of a write to 0x4 (INTR_ENABLE) with o_d_error=0, shadow_en=data. For each i: if shadow_en[i]=0 and the edge is at least Ed+2 after the last INTR_ENABLE write (or no write since reset), then o_intr_gpio[i]=0. The check is disabled from an A handshake with i_a_intg_flip=1 until rst_ni=0.

checks.title: Interrupt level is held until software acknowledges it
checks.behavior: For each i: if o_intr_gpio[i]=1 at rising edge N and o_intr_gpio[i]=0 at N+1 with rst_ni=1 at both edges, then a qualifying write must be in progress around N+1. A qualifying write is either a write to 0x0 (INTR_STATE) with i_a_data[i]=1 or a write to 0x4 (INTR_ENABLE) with i_a_data[i]=0. Its A handshake must be at or before N+1, and its D handshake must be at or after N-1 or not yet done. In other words, only a software W1C or a software mask can lower an asserted interrupt; hardware never clears it. The check is disabled from an A handshake with i_a_intg_flip=1 until rst_ni=0.

checks.title: Outputs held at zero during reset
checks.behavior: At every rising edge and every falling edge of clk_i at which rst_ni=0, all of these must be 0: o_d_valid, o_alert, o_alert_integ_fail, o_intr_gpio (32'h0), o_gpio (32'h0) and o_gpio_en (32'h0). This includes the first clock edge after rst_ni falls asynchronously. o_a_ready, o_straps_valid and o_straps_data are not checked.

checks.title: Strap outputs: invalid before the trigger, frozen after sampling
checks.behavior:
Only when GpioAsHwStrapsEn=1.
(a) At every rising edge with rst_ni=1 where i_strap_en has been 0 at every rising edge since reset release: o_straps_valid=0.
(b) If o_straps_valid=1 at rising edge N with rst_ni=1, and rst_ni=1 at N+1, then at N+1 o_straps_valid=1 and o_straps_data equals its value at N, whatever i_gpio and i_strap_en do.

checks.title: Outputs change only at rising clock edges
checks.behavior: Every change of any output (o_a_ready, o_d_*, o_d_intg_err, o_alert, o_alert_integ_fail, o_gpio, o_gpio_en, o_intr_gpio, o_straps_valid, o_straps_data) happens in the simulation time step of a rising edge of clk_i. Equivalently, each output sampled at a falling edge of clk_i equals its value sampled just before the next rising edge. Not applied in clock cycles where rst_ni is 0 or falls.

checks.title: Test-bench stimulus legality monitor (host rules and plan constraints)
checks.behavior:
This monitor checks the stimulus and flags test-bench errors, not DUT errors.
(a) If at rising edge N rst_ni=1, i_a_valid=1 and o_a_ready=0, then at N+1: i_a_valid=1, and i_a_opcode, i_a_param, i_a_size, i_a_source, i_a_address, i_a_mask, i_a_data, i_a_instr and i_a_intg_flip are unchanged.
(b) i_a_valid=0 at every edge with rst_ni=0 and at the first rising edge after rst_ni rises.
(c) No A handshake uses an i_a_source equal to that of a request still outstanding.
(d) Whenever i_a_valid=1: i_a_address<32'h400; not (i_a_instr=1 and i_a_opcode in {0,1}); i_a_mask is in {0001,0010,0100,1000,0011,1100,1111}; and i_a_opcode=0 implies i_a_size=2.
(e) If GpioAsHwStrapsEn=1: i_strap_en=0 while rst_ni=0 and at the first 4 rising edges after release. Let Es be the first rising edge after release at which i_strap_en=1. i_gpio has the same value at every rising edge from Es-24 to Es+8.
(f) If GpioAsyncOn=0: every input, i_gpio included, has the same value at each falling edge of clk_i as at the following rising edge, i.e. it changes only just after rising edges.

checks.title: D channel held stable under back-pressure
checks.behavior: If at rising edge N rst_ni=1, o_d_valid=1 and i_d_ready=0, and rst_ni is still 1 at rising edge N+1, then at N+1: o_d_valid=1, and o_d_opcode, o_d_param, o_d_size, o_d_source, o_d_sink, o_d_data and o_d_error equal their values at N.

checks.title: Response matches an outstanding request (source/size/opcode echo, no orphans)
checks.behavior:
The checker records each A handshake: a rising edge with rst_ni=1, i_a_valid=1 and o_a_ready=1. It stores i_a_source, i_a_size and i_a_opcode. At each D handshake (a rising edge with rst_ni=1, o_d_valid=1 and i_d_ready=1):
- Exactly one recorded entry accepted at an earlier edge and not yet answered must have a_source equal to o_d_source. That entry is removed, so every request gets exactly one response beat.
- If the stored opcode is 4 (Get): o_d_opcode=1 (AccessAckData) and o_d_size equals the stored a_size.
- If the stored opcode is 0 or 1: o_d_opcode=0 (AccessAck) and o_d_size equals the stored a_size.
- If the stored opcode is 2, 3, 5, 6 or 7: only o_d_error=1 is checked.
- A D handshake with no matching entry is a failure (orphan response).
All entries are cleared at any edge where rst_ni=0, so a D beat after reset for a request accepted before reset is an orphan (the pending response must be discarded). The checker is disabled from an A handshake with i_a_intg_flip=1 until the next rst_ni=0. o_d_param and o_d_sink are not checked.

checks.title: ALERT_TEST.fatal_fault triggers exactly one o_alert pulse
checks.behavior: Each write of 1 to ALERT_TEST.fatal_fault, with regwen kept at 1, causes exactly one o_alert pulse within 16 cycles of the write response.
checks.stimulus: Three times, separated by at least 64 idle cycles: write ALERT_TEST=32'h8000_0001 (never 32'h0000_0001) with no other alert cause, then observe 64 cycles. Finally read ALERT_TEST.
checks.expected:
- Each write completes with d_error=0.
- After each write, exactly one o_alert pulse (1 for one cycle) occurs no later than 16 cycles after the D handshake, and no other pulse occurs in the 64-cycle window.
- ALERT_TEST reads 32'h8000_0000. o_alert_integ_fail stays 0.

checks.title: ALERT_TEST.regwen rw0c locks alert testing until reset
checks.behavior: Writing 0 to regwen disables alert testing until the next reset.
checks.stimulus:
1. After reset, read ALERT_TEST.
2. Write ALERT_TEST=32'h0000_0000 and read it.
3. Write ALERT_TEST=32'h8000_0001, observe 64 cycles, and read it.
4. Assert rst_ni for 10 cycles and release it. Read ALERT_TEST, write 32'h8000_0001, and observe 64 cycles.
checks.expected:
- Step 1 reads 32'h8000_0000.
- Step 2 reads 32'h0000_0000.
- Step 3: the write gives d_error=0, no o_alert pulse occurs in the 64 cycles, and ALERT_TEST still reads 32'h0000_0000.
- Step 4: ALERT_TEST reads 32'h8000_0000, and the write gives exactly one o_alert pulse within 16 cycles of its response.

checks.title: Command integrity error raises the fatal alert, repeated until reset
checks.behavior: A request with corrupted command integrity starts the fatal alert, which repeats until reset and stops after reset.
checks.stimulus:
1. Run normal traffic (i_a_intg_flip=0) for 100 cycles.
2. Send one Get to 0x10 with i_a_intg_flip=1 and a unique a_source (in a second run, a PutFullData to 0x14). Wait at most 32 cycles for its response.
3. Observe 512 cycles.
4. Assert rst_ni for 10 cycles and release it.
5. Run 256 cycles of normal traffic with i_a_intg_flip=0.
checks.expected:
- No o_alert pulse during step 1.
- After the flipped request is accepted at edge Ea, the first o_alert pulse occurs at or before Ea+16. Then there are never 32 consecutive rising edges without an o_alert pulse until rst_ni falls.
- The response, its effect on registers and later requests are not checked.
- o_alert=0 while rst_ni=0.
- After release, there is no o_alert pulse in the 256 cycles, normal accesses give d_error=0, and registers read their reset values.
- o_alert_integ_fail and o_d_intg_err stay 0.

checks.title: Input noise filter on DATA_IN and interrupt detection
checks.behavior: With the filter on, a pulse of at most 12 cycles is filtered out of DATA_IN and interrupt detection, and a change held for at least 24 cycles gets through. The filter is set per bit.
checks.stimulus:
Bits under test: i in {0,15,16,31}; j=i^1 is the companion bit with the filter off.
1. Hold i_gpio=0. Write CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER = (1<<i), INTR_CTRL_EN_RISING = INTR_CTRL_EN_FALLING = (1<<i)|(1<<j), INTR_ENABLE = (1<<i)|(1<<j). Wait 24 cycles with i_gpio constant. Clear INTR_STATE by writing 32'hFFFF_FFFF.
2. Short pulse: drive i_gpio[i] and i_gpio[j] to 1 for exactly 12 cycles (E0..E0+11), then back to 0. Poll DATA_IN back-to-back from E0 to E0+50.
3. Long change: drive i_gpio[i] to 1 and hold it for 40 cycles from edge E1. Read DATA_IN accepted at E1+24 or later, and INTR_STATE accepted at E1+28 or later.
checks.expected:
- Step 2:
  - DATA_IN[i] reads 0 in every poll, INTR_STATE[i] reads 0, and o_intr_gpio[i]=0 throughout.
  - Bit j (filter off) reads 1 in DATA_IN for polls accepted between E0+4 and E0+11, and INTR_STATE[j]=1 for reads accepted at E0+8 or later.
- Step 3:
  - DATA_IN[i] reads 1 for reads accepted at E1+24 or later.
  - INTR_STATE[i] reads 1 for reads accepted at E1+28 or later.
  - o_intr_gpio[i]=1 from E1+30.
- All responses have d_error=0.

checks.title: Direct write of DATA_OUT through DIRECT_OUT
checks.behavior: DIRECT_OUT writes and reads all 32 bits of DATA_OUT at once, and o_gpio follows.
checks.stimulus: Write DIRECT_OUT with: 32'h0000_0001 shifted left by k for k=0..31 (walking ones), 32'hFFFF_FFFF, 32'h0, and 50 random 32-bit values. After each write, read DIRECT_OUT (0x14), MASKED_OUT_LOWER (0x18) and MASKED_OUT_UPPER (0x1C).
checks.expected:
Let V be the value written.
- DIRECT_OUT reads V.
- MASKED_OUT_LOWER reads {16'h0, V[15:0]}.
- MASKED_OUT_UPPER reads {16'h0, V[31:16]}.
- o_gpio==V at every rising edge from 2 cycles after the write's D handshake until the next write.
- All responses have d_error=0.

checks.title: Masked writes of DATA_OUT through MASKED_OUT_LOWER / MASKED_OUT_UPPER
checks.behavior: A masked write changes only the bits whose mask bit is 1. Reads return the selected half of DATA_OUT in bits 15:0 and zero in the mask field.
checks.stimulus:
1. Write DIRECT_OUT=32'h1234_5678.
2. Write MASKED_OUT_LOWER=32'h00FF_ABCD.
3. Write MASKED_OUT_UPPER=32'hF0F0_FFFF.
4. Write MASKED_OUT_LOWER=32'h0000_FFFF (mask 0).
5. Write MASKED_OUT_UPPER=32'h0000_0000 (mask 0).
6. Run 100 random masked writes to either register with random mask and data.
Read DIRECT_OUT, MASKED_OUT_LOWER and MASKED_OUT_UPPER after each write.
checks.expected:
- After step 2: DIRECT_OUT=32'h1234_56CD.
- After step 3: DIRECT_OUT=32'hF2F4_56CD.
- After steps 4 and 5: DIRECT_OUT unchanged at 32'hF2F4_56CD; MASKED_OUT_LOWER reads 32'h0000_56CD and MASKED_OUT_UPPER reads 32'h0000_F2F4.
- Random writes: DATA_OUT[h*16+i]=data[i] where mask[i]=1 and is unchanged where mask[i]=0 (h=0 for LOWER, 1 for UPPER). MASKED_OUT_* bits 31:16 always read 0.
- o_gpio equals the expected DATA_OUT from 2 cycles after each write response.
- All responses have d_error=0.

checks.title: DATA_OE: direct and masked writes, reads and o_gpio_en
checks.behavior: DATA_OE has the same direct and masked write semantics as DATA_OUT, and o_gpio_en follows DATA_OE.
checks.stimulus:
1. Write DIRECT_OE (0x20) with walking ones, 32'hFFFF_FFFF, 32'h0 and random values.
2. Write DIRECT_OE=32'h1234_5678, then MASKED_OE_LOWER (0x24)=32'h00FF_ABCD, then MASKED_OE_UPPER (0x28)=32'hF0F0_FFFF, then mask-0 writes to both.
3. Run 100 random masked writes.
Read DIRECT_OE, MASKED_OE_LOWER and MASKED_OE_UPPER after each write.
checks.expected:
- After each DIRECT_OE write of V: DIRECT_OE reads V, and o_gpio_en==V from 2 cycles after the response. Each bit i set to 1 gives o_gpio_en[i]=1.
- The step 2 sequence gives DATA_OE=32'h1234_56CD, then 32'hF2F4_56CD, then unchanged after the mask-0 writes.
- Random masked writes update only bits whose mask is 1.
- Bits 15:0 of MASKED_OE_LOWER equal DATA_OE[15:0], and bits 15:0 of MASKED_OE_UPPER equal DATA_OE[31:16]. Bits 31:16 of MASKED_OE_* reads are not checked.
- o_gpio_en equals the expected DATA_OE from 2 cycles after each write response. o_gpio is not affected.
- d_error=0 on every response.

checks.title: DATA_IN with filter off follows i_gpio only (both GpioAsyncOn values)
checks.behavior: With the filter off, a held change of i_gpio shows in DATA_IN within 4 cycles, whatever DATA_OUT and DATA_OE are.
checks.stimulus:
1. CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER=0. Write DIRECT_OE=32'hFFFF_FFFF.
2. Drive i_gpio with walking ones, walking zeros and 100 random values, each held for at least 8 cycles. Before each new value V, write DIRECT_OUT=~V.
3. With GpioAsyncOn=1, change i_gpio at random times within the clock period. With GpioAsyncOn=0, change it only just after rising edges.
4. Let E0 be the first rising edge at which i_gpio has the new value. Send a Get of DATA_IN accepted at E0+4 or later (before the next change), and a Get of PER_PIN_IO_i for i in {0,15,16,31}.
5. Repeat with DIRECT_OE=0.
checks.expected:
- DATA_IN reads V, not o_gpio and not DATA_OUT.
- PER_PIN_IO_i bit 8 equals V[i].
- d_error=0. Identical results with DIRECT_OE=32'hFFFF_FFFF and with DIRECT_OE=0.

checks.title: Edge interrupts: rising, falling, both; latching, W1C, raw INTR_STATE
checks.behavior: A configured edge on GPIO i sets INTR_STATE[i] within the D-018 bound and raises o_intr_gpio[i]. The interrupt stays latched until a W1C write, and INTR_STATE is not masked by INTR_ENABLE.
checks.stimulus:
Filter off. For i in {0,15,16,31} and 4 random bits:
1. Rising: i_gpio=0. Write INTR_CTRL_EN_RISING=(1<<i), others 0, and INTR_ENABLE=(1<<i). Drive i_gpio[i] 0->1 at E0 and hold for 20 cycles. Read INTR_STATE at E0+8 or later. Drive i_gpio[i] 1->0, hold 20 cycles, read INTR_STATE. Write INTR_STATE=~(1<<i), read it. Write INTR_STATE=(1<<i), read it.
2. Falling: the same with INTR_CTRL_EN_FALLING and the opposite edges.
3. Both: RISING and FALLING both set on bit i. Rise, then W1C, then fall.
4. Raw state: after an event with INTR_ENABLE[i]=1, write INTR_ENABLE=0 and read INTR_STATE.
checks.expected:
- Rising, step 1:
  - INTR_STATE reads exactly (1<<i) for reads accepted at E0+8 or later.
  - o_intr_gpio=(1<<i) from E0+10.
  - After the falling input, INTR_STATE[i] still reads 1 and o_intr_gpio[i] stays 1 (not cleared by hardware).
  - The W1C write of ~(1<<i) leaves INTR_STATE=(1<<i).
  - The W1C write of (1<<i) makes INTR_STATE read 0 and o_intr_gpio[i]=0 from 2 cycles after the response.
  - The opposite (falling) edge alone never sets INTR_STATE[i].
- Falling, step 2: the mirror image of step 1.
- Both edges, step 3: each edge sets INTR_STATE[i]=1. INTR_STATE is identical for both edges.
- Raw state, step 4: INTR_STATE[i] still reads 1, and o_intr_gpio[i]=0 from 2 cycles after the INTR_ENABLE write response.
- At all times outside the 2 cycles after a change of INTR_STATE or INTR_ENABLE, o_intr_gpio equals INTR_STATE & INTR_ENABLE.

checks.title: Level interrupts: high, low, and W1C while the level holds
checks.behavior: A configured level sets INTR_STATE[i]. A W1C write while the level still holds does not clear the interrupt for good.
checks.stimulus:
Filter off. For i in {0,15,16,31}:
1. LVLHIGH: i_gpio[i]=0. Write INTR_CTRL_EN_LVLHIGH=(1<<i), others 0, and INTR_ENABLE=(1<<i). Drive i_gpio[i]=1 at E0 and keep it. Read INTR_STATE at E0+8 or later. Write INTR_STATE=(1<<i) while i_gpio[i] is still 1, then read INTR_STATE. Drive i_gpio[i]=0, wait 8 cycles, write INTR_STATE=(1<<i), read INTR_STATE, observe 64 cycles.
2. LVLLOW: the mirror image (start at 1, configure LVLLOW, drive 0).
checks.expected:
- INTR_STATE[i] reads 1 for reads accepted at E0+8 or later, and o_intr_gpio[i]=1 from E0+10.
- After the W1C while the level holds, INTR_STATE[i] reads 1 and o_intr_gpio[i]=1 from 4 cycles after that write's response onward. A dip in between is not checked.
- After the level is removed and W1C is written, INTR_STATE[i] reads 0, and o_intr_gpio[i]=0 from 2 cycles after the response and for the next 64 cycles.
- LVLLOW behaves the same way.

checks.title: INTR_TEST forcing and INTR_ENABLE masking per bit
checks.behavior: INTR_TEST forces INTR_STATE bits, INTR_ENABLE masks o_intr_gpio bit by bit, and each GPIO has its own interrupt line.
checks.stimulus:
All INTR_CTRL_EN_* =0, i_gpio constant.
1. Write INTR_ENABLE=32'hFFFF_FFFF, then INTR_TEST=32'h8001_0001. Read INTR_STATE and INTR_TEST.
2. Write INTR_ENABLE=32'h0000_0001. Read INTR_STATE.
3. Write INTR_STATE=32'hFFFF_FFFF and read it.
4. Write INTR_ENABLE=0. Set INTR_CTRL_EN_RISING and INTR_CTRL_EN_FALLING to 32'hFFFF_FFFF and toggle i_gpio with random values held for 8 or more cycles, for 200 cycles.
5. Return the CTRL registers to 0. Write INTR_STATE=32'hFFFF_FFFF, then INTR_ENABLE=32'hFFFF_FFFF, and wait 4 cycles.
checks.expected:
- Step 1: INTR_STATE reads 32'h8001_0001, INTR_TEST reads 0, and o_intr_gpio=32'h8001_0001 from 2 cycles after the INTR_TEST write response.
- Step 2: o_intr_gpio=32'h0000_0001 from 2 cycles after the response. INTR_STATE still reads 32'h8001_0001.
- Step 3: INTR_STATE reads 0 and o_intr_gpio=0 from 2 cycles after the response.
- Step 4: o_intr_gpio=0 at every edge. INTR_STATE is not checked.
- Step 5: o_intr_gpio=0 from 4 cycles after the INTR_ENABLE write response.

checks.title: PER_PIN_IO_i aliases DATA_OUT[i] / DATA_IN[i] and affects only GPIO i
checks.behavior: Each PER_PIN_IO_i register shows and writes only GPIO i, and aliases the same state as the 32-bit registers.
checks.stimulus:
i_gpio=G=32'h6B2D_94C1, held constant. For every i in 0..31 (this includes 0, 15, 16 and 31):
1. Write DIRECT_OUT=P (P is random, and also 32'h0 and 32'hFFFF_FFFF).
2. Write PER_PIN_IO_i (0x100+4*i) with full-word data 32'h1 if P[i]=0, else 32'h0.
3. Read DIRECT_OUT, DIRECT_OE, INTR_ENABLE and PER_PIN_IO_j for j in {i, (i+1)%32}.
4. Write DIRECT_OUT with bit i inverted and read PER_PIN_IO_i.
PER_PIN_IO writes are always full-word (PutFullData, mask 1111).
checks.expected:
- After step 2, DIRECT_OUT = P with only bit i inverted, and o_gpio equals that value from 2 cycles after the response.
- DIRECT_OE and INTR_ENABLE are unchanged.
- PER_PIN_IO_i reads (G[i]<<8)|DATA_OUT[i], with all other bits 0.
- PER_PIN_IO_(i+1) shows its own DATA_OUT and G bits.
- After step 4, PER_PIN_IO_i bit 0 equals the new DATA_OUT[i].
- d_error=0 on every response.

checks.title: PER_PIN_OE_i / PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_i alias their bit and affect only GPIO i
checks.behavior: Each per-pin configuration register aliases bit i of DATA_OE or of the interrupt-control and filter registers, and a write to it changes only GPIO i.
checks.stimulus:
INTR_ENABLE=0 and i_gpio constant. For every i in 0..31:
1. Write DIRECT_OE=random R. Write PER_PIN_OE_i (0x200+8*i) full-word with ~R[i]. Read DIRECT_OE and PER_PIN_OE_i.
2. Preload INTR_CTRL_EN_RISING/FALLING/LVLHIGH/LVLLOW and CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER with random values. Write PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_i (0x204+8*i) with 32'h01, 32'h02, 32'h04, 32'h08, 32'h10, 32'h1F and 32'h00 in turn. After each write, wait 24 cycles and read 0x2C, 0x30, 0x34, 0x38 and 0x3C.
3. Write the five 32-bit registers with random values and read PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_i and PER_PIN_OE_i.
checks.expected:
- After step 1, DIRECT_OE = R with bit i inverted, PER_PIN_OE_i reads that bit in bit 0 with other bits 0, and o_gpio_en follows within 2 cycles after the response.
- In step 2, bit i of INTR_CTRL_EN_RISING, FALLING, LVLHIGH, LVLLOW and CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER equals bits 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4 of the written value. All other bits of these registers keep their preloaded value.
- In step 3, PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_i reads {27'h0, FILTER[i], LVLLOW[i], LVLHIGH[i], FALLING[i], RISING[i]} and PER_PIN_OE_i reads {31'h0, DATA_OE[i]}.
- d_error=0 on every response.

checks.title: Interrupt registers have no per-pin view
checks.behavior: Writes to the per-pin ranges never change INTR_STATE, INTR_ENABLE or INTR_TEST.
checks.stimulus:
1. Write INTR_ENABLE=32'hFFFF_FFFF. Keep INTR_CTRL_EN_LVLHIGH and INTR_CTRL_EN_LVLLOW at 0, and i_gpio=0 constant.
2. For i in {0,15,16,31}: write PER_PIN_IO_i=32'hFFFF_FFFF, PER_PIN_OE_i=32'hFFFF_FFFF and PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_i=32'h0000_0001 (rising only; the input does not change).
3. Read INTR_STATE, INTR_ENABLE and INTR_TEST.
checks.expected:
- INTR_STATE reads 0, INTR_ENABLE reads 32'hFFFF_FFFF and INTR_TEST reads 0.
- o_intr_gpio=0 throughout.
- All writes complete with d_error=0.

checks.title: Reset values of every register
checks.behavior: Right after reset, every register at its specified offset returns its reset value.
checks.stimulus:
In each configuration of the run set:
1. Hold rst_ni=0 for 10 cycles with i_a_valid=0, i_strap_en=0 and i_gpio=32'hA5A5_5A5A constant. Release rst_ni synchronously.
2. Wait 20 cycles.
3. Issue a Get (a_opcode=4, a_size=2, a_mask=1111) to every offset 0x00..0x44 in steps of 4, to 0x100..0x17C (PER_PIN_IO_0..31) and to 0x200..0x2FC (PER_PIN_OE_i at 0x200+8*i, PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_i at 0x204+8*i). Use no writes before these reads.
checks.expected:
Every response has d_error=0.
- ALERT_TEST (0xC) reads 32'h8000_0000.
- DATA_IN (0x10) reads 32'hA5A5_5A5A.
- PER_PIN_IO_i reads ({i_gpio[i]}<<8), i.e. bit 8 = bit i of 32'hA5A5_5A5A and all other bits 0.
- HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN_VALID (0x40) reads 0 when GpioAsHwStrapsEn=1 (not checked when it is 0).
- HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN (0x44) reads 0.
- Every other register reads 32'h0: INTR_STATE, INTR_ENABLE, INTR_TEST, DIRECT_OUT, MASKED_OUT_LOWER/UPPER, DIRECT_OE, MASKED_OE_LOWER/UPPER (bits 15:0 checked), INTR_CTRL_EN_RISING/FALLING/LVLHIGH/LVLLOW, CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER, all PER_PIN_OE_i and all PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_i.
- o_gpio=0, o_gpio_en=0 and o_intr_gpio=0 throughout. o_alert never pulses.

checks.title: Field access types: rw, wo, ro, rw0c, reserved bits; RACL off
checks.behavior: Each register field behaves as its access type says, and every legal full-word access is accepted.
checks.stimulus:
i_gpio=32'h3C3C_C3C3 constant. INTR_ENABLE=0 and all INTR_CTRL_EN_* =0 unless written below. All writes are PutFullData with a_size=2, a_mask=1111.
1. For each rw register (INTR_ENABLE 0x4, DIRECT_OUT 0x14, DIRECT_OE 0x20, INTR_CTRL_EN_RISING 0x2C, FALLING 0x30, LVLHIGH 0x34, LVLLOW 0x38, CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER 0x3C), write and read back 32'hFFFF_FFFF, 32'h0, 32'hA5A5_5A5A and 32'h5A5A_A5A5. Restore 0 at the end; wait 24 cycles after each CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER write before reading DATA_IN.
2. Write INTR_TEST=32'h0 and read it.
3. Write ALERT_TEST=32'hFFFF_FFFE (bit 31=1, bit 0=0) and read it.
4. Write DATA_IN=32'hFFFF_FFFF, then 32'h0, reading after each.
5. Write HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN_VALID=32'hFFFF_FFFF and HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN=32'hFFFF_FFFF, reading before and after.
6. For i in {0,15,16,31}, write PER_PIN_IO_i=32'hFFFF_FFFF, PER_PIN_OE_i=32'hFFFF_FFFF and PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_i=32'hFFFF_FFFF, then read them.
7. Write MASKED_OUT_LOWER=32'hFFFF_FFFF and read it.
checks.expected:
- All accesses complete with d_error=0 (no access-control rejection).
- rw registers read back exactly the value written.
- INTR_TEST reads 0.
- ALERT_TEST reads 32'h8000_0000: wo bit 0 and reserved bits 30:1 read 0, regwen is still 1. No o_alert pulse occurs.
- DATA_IN still reads 32'h3C3C_C3C3.
- HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN_VALID and HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN read the same as before the writes.
- PER_PIN_IO_i reads ((bit i of 32'h3C3C_C3C3)<<8)|1. PER_PIN_OE_i reads 32'h1. PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_i reads 32'h1F.
- MASKED_OUT_LOWER reads 32'h0000_FFFF (the wo mask field reads 0).

checks.title: Asynchronous reset assertion, short reset and discarding of a pending response
checks.behavior: Reset is asserted asynchronously and released synchronously. It clears the outputs and the registers, drops any pending response, and works even when it lasts only 2 cycles.
checks.stimulus:
1. Write DIRECT_OUT=32'hFFFF_FFFF and DIRECT_OE=32'hFFFF_FFFF. Write INTR_ENABLE=32'hFFFF_FFFF and INTR_TEST=32'hFFFF_FFFF.
2. Set i_d_ready=0 and send a Get to 0x14, holding it until o_d_valid=1.
3. Assert rst_ni=0 a quarter clock period after a rising edge and keep it low for only 2 rising edges. Release it synchronously.
4. Keep i_a_valid=0 during reset and for the first cycle after release, with i_d_ready=1, and observe 20 cycles without new requests.
5. Read DIRECT_OUT, DIRECT_OE, INTR_ENABLE and INTR_STATE.
checks.expected:
- At the first falling edge of clk_i after rst_ni falls (before the next rising edge), and while rst_ni=0: o_gpio=0, o_gpio_en=0, o_intr_gpio=0, o_d_valid=0, o_alert=0 and o_alert_integ_fail=0.
- After release, no o_d_valid occurs in the 20 idle cycles: the pending response is discarded.
- Then the reads all return 0 with d_error=0, and normal accesses work after the short reset.

checks.title: Strap sampling with GpioAsHwStrapsEn=1 (once per reset, regardless of OE)
checks.behavior: Runs only in the configurations with GpioAsHwStrapsEn=1. The first rising edge of i_strap_en after reset samples i_gpio into HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN, and later changes have no effect until the next reset.
checks.stimulus:
1. Hold i_strap_en=0 while rst_ni=0 and for 10 cycles after release.
2. Write DIRECT_OE=32'hFFFF_FFFF and DIRECT_OUT=32'h0F0F_0F0F.
3. Drive i_gpio=S=32'h3C5A_A5C3 from at least 24 cycles before raising i_strap_en.
4. Read HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN_VALID (0x40) before raising i_strap_en.
5. Raise i_strap_en. Es is the first rising edge with i_strap_en=1. Keep i_gpio=S until Es+8.
6. Read 0x40 and 0x44 accepted at Es+4 or later.
7. Drive random i_gpio values and toggle i_strap_en 5 times over 200 cycles, reading 0x40 and 0x44 again.
8. Reset, then repeat steps 1 to 7 with S2=32'hC3A5_5A3C.
checks.expected:
- Before Es: 0x40 reads 0 and o_straps_valid=0.
- From Es+4 on: o_straps_valid=1 and o_straps_data=S. 0x40 reads 32'h1 and 0x44 reads S. The value does not depend on DATA_OE or DATA_OUT.
- In step 7, o_straps_valid, o_straps_data, 0x40 and 0x44 stay unchanged at 1 and S.
- After the reset in step 8, the new sample is S2 with the same timing.
- All responses have d_error=0.

checks.title: HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN reads zero when GpioAsHwStrapsEn=0
checks.behavior: Runs only in the configurations with GpioAsHwStrapsEn=0. HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN reads 0 at all times.
checks.stimulus: Use the same stimulus as CHK-031 steps 1 to 7 with S=32'h3C5A_A5C3. Read HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN (0x44) before the i_strap_en rise, at Es+4 or later, and after the random i_gpio and i_strap_en changes.
checks.expected:
- 0x44 reads 32'h0 in every read, with d_error=0.
- HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN_VALID, o_straps_valid and o_straps_data are not checked.

checks.title: Aligned byte writes: rejected on wide registers, accepted on PER_PIN_OE / PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL
checks.behavior: A byte write to a register with fields above bit 7 is an error with no effect. A byte write to PER_PIN_OE_i or PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_i succeeds.
checks.stimulus:
1. Preload: DIRECT_OUT=32'h5555_AAAA, DIRECT_OE=32'hAAAA_5555, INTR_ENABLE=32'hFFFF_FFFF, all INTR_CTRL_EN_* =32'h0F0F_0F0F with i_gpio constant (no events), CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER=32'h0. Write INTR_TEST=32'h0000_0100 so INTR_STATE=32'h0000_0100.
2. Send PutPartialData (a_opcode=1, a_size=0, a_mask=0001, address = register offset, data 32'h0000_00FF) to INTR_STATE, INTR_ENABLE, INTR_TEST, DIRECT_OUT, MASKED_OUT_LOWER, MASKED_OUT_UPPER, DIRECT_OE, MASKED_OE_LOWER, MASKED_OE_UPPER, the four INTR_CTRL_EN_* registers, CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER and PER_PIN_IO_i for i in {0,15,16,31}. Read every register after each write.
3. Send byte writes with the same encoding to PER_PIN_OE_i (data 8'h01, then 8'h00) and PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_i (data 8'h1F, then 8'h00) for i in {0,15,16,31}.
checks.expected:
- Every step-2 write gives d_error=1. All register reads are unchanged: INTR_STATE stays 32'h0000_0100, and DIRECT_OUT, DIRECT_OE, INTR_ENABLE and the INTR_CTRL_EN_* registers keep their preloaded values.
- o_gpio, o_gpio_en and o_intr_gpio (=32'h0000_0100) are unchanged.
- Every step-3 write gives d_error=0 and takes effect: DIRECT_OE[i] becomes 1 then 0, and bit i of all five control registers becomes 1 then 0, with readback and o_gpio_en as in CHK-026.

checks.title: Sub-word reads return the full register
checks.behavior: Reads smaller than a word are accepted and return the whole register, with each byte in its own lane.
checks.stimulus:
1. Write DIRECT_OUT=32'hF2F4_56CD.
2. Send Gets to DIRECT_OUT with (a_size=0, address 0x14, mask 0001), (a_size=0, address 0x17, mask 1000), (a_size=1, address 0x16, mask 1100) and (a_size=1, address 0x14, mask 0011).
checks.expected: Every response has d_error=0, o_d_data=32'hF2F4_56CD, and o_d_size equal to the request's a_size.

checks.title: TL-UL protocol error cases answered with d_error=1
checks.behavior: Requests with an undefined opcode, too large a size, a misaligned address or a mask covering inactive lanes are answered with d_error=1 and change nothing.
checks.expected:
- (a) to (e) all give d_error=1. For (a), only d_error is checked.
- For (b) to (e), d_source and d_size echo the request (CHK-013).
- DIRECT_OUT reads 0 and o_gpio stays 0 throughout. No o_alert pulse.

checks.title: Unmapped offsets return d_error=1 and change nothing
checks.behavior: Accesses to unmapped offsets below 0x400 are errors and have no effect.
checks.stimulus:
1. Preload every rw register with distinct non-zero patterns (INTR_ENABLE=32'h0, i_gpio constant).
2. Send a Get, then a PutFullData with data 32'hFFFF_FFFF, to each of 0x048, 0x04C, 0x080, 0x0FC, 0x180, 0x1FC, 0x300 and 0x3FC. All addresses are below 0x400.
3. Read all mapped registers.
checks.expected:
- Every request to these offsets gives d_error=1.
- All mapped registers read their preloaded values, and o_gpio and o_gpio_en are unchanged.

checks.title: Instruction-fetch reads complete without side effects
checks.behavior: Reads marked as instruction fetches get a response and change nothing.
checks.stimulus:
1. Write DIRECT_OUT=32'hCAFE_0001.
2. Send Gets with i_a_instr=1 to 0x14 and 0x10. No write is sent with i_a_instr=1.
3. Read DIRECT_OUT with i_a_instr=0.
checks.expected:
- Each instruction-fetch Get gets exactly one response with d_source, d_size and d_opcode=1 as in CHK-013. d_error and d_data are not checked.
- DIRECT_OUT then reads 32'hCAFE_0001, o_gpio is unchanged, and o_alert does not pulse.

checks.title: Outstanding requests and back-pressure
checks.behavior: The device handles back-to-back requests and D-channel back-pressure, and every response carries the right source and data.
checks.stimulus:
Run 500 random legal full-word reads and writes to mapped rw registers.
- Each request uses a distinct a_source among outstanding requests; values include 8'h00, 8'h01, 8'h7F, 8'hFF and random values.
- i_a_valid is asserted back-to-back whenever possible and held until o_a_ready=1, with no assumption that o_a_ready is 1.
- i_d_ready is randomly deasserted for 0 to 10 cycles.
checks.expected:
- Every request gets exactly one response, matched by d_source.
- Read data equals a reference model of the register values (writes applied in acceptance order).
- d_error=0 on all responses. CHK-012 and CHK-013 hold throughout.

not_verified.note: There is no pad model (INT-IO-002, D-021). i_gpio comes only from the test bench, so output-to-input delay does not occur. Designer decision for GP-T2.2-05/06.
Software capability-assignment advice; nothing to observe.
Ping requests belong to the wrapper's internal alert receiver. No port shows them.
a_user.rsvd is set inside the wrapper and is not a port.
D-012: requests at 0x400 and above are not used, so stripping of excess address bits is not exercised.
D-013 limits sub-word write checks to aligned byte writes (CHK-033). Unaligned sub-word writes are explicitly not checked.
Software/hardware priority in the same internal cycle cannot be lined up from the ports without knowing internal latency.
Same-cycle de/we collision is internal timing.
Structure of the hwext register bundle.
Whether a ro register is hwext/hardwired is an implementation attribute. The read value of HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN with straps disabled is checked in CHK-032.
Simultaneous hardware/software write to a rw1c subreg needs internal cycle alignment. The visible W1C behaviour is covered by CHK-022/CHK-023.
MAY about reuse of IP blocks.
gpio is not a baseline block; it uses the a_user integrity fields.
gpio is not a baseline block.
Relaxation for host drivers. The test bench follows D-016 (CHK-011).
Interconnect routing rule. There is no fabric in ot_gpio_nnc.
Bus primitive source-ID growth. There is no primitive between the test bench and the DUT.
Host rule about source contraction through a fabric. The DUT is connected directly; CHK-013 checks the full 8-bit d_source echo.
MAY. Non-contiguous masks are not driven (TL-T3.1.3.4-02, CHK-011), and D-013 leaves partial masks unchecked.
Presence of a device interface (the TL-UL ports exist).
gpio is not a bus host.
Clocking structure. The single test-bench host runs on clk_i.
Port naming of the inner module.
hjson key option. All gpio interrupts are event type.
Status-type interrupts. All gpio interrupts are event type (designer decision).
Status-type interrupts are out of scope (designer decision).
Status-type interrupt masking. Masking for event interrupts is checked in CHK-006/CHK-024.
gpio has no recoverable alert, only fatal_fault.
Instantiation and IsFatal parameter. The fatal repeat behaviour is checked in CHK-016.
gpio has no recoverable alerts or cause registers.
gpio has no fatal alert cause register.
The differential pair is internal. Correct encoding is seen through o_alert pulses and o_alert_integ_fail=0 (CHK-001, CHK-014, CHK-016).
Sender and receiver share clk_i in the wrapper; there is no asynchronous boundary.
The handshake pause is inside the diff-pair protocol. Only the bounds on o_alert pulse spacing are checked (CHK-016).
Designer decision: sender-side encoding error signalling is not observable except via o_alert_integ_fail, which must stay 0 (CHK-001).
Designer decision: no ping requests (INT-CFG-003), so pingfail and lock-up are not checked.

assumptions: The T5.1 register-table quote is cut off after MASKED_OUT_UPPER (0x1C). The remaining offsets are assumed to follow the gpio register order: DIRECT_OE 0x20, MASKED_OE_LOWER 0x24, MASKED_OE_UPPER 0x28, INTR_CTRL_EN_RISING 0x2C, INTR_CTRL_EN_FALLING 0x30, INTR_CTRL_EN_LVLHIGH 0x34, INTR_CTRL_EN_LVLLOW 0x38, CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER 0x3C, HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN_VALID 0x40, HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN 0x44. This is consistent with GP-T5.1-01: 18 registers from 0x0 to 0x44.
HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN_VALID has its single field at bit 0, with all other bits reserved (read 0). HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN resets to 0x0 before any strap sample. Its field tables are not in the rules.

Cycle counts are rising edges of clk_i. E0 is the first rising edge at which a changed input is already present, as in the designer decision for D-018. A read 'accepted at Ex' means its A handshake (i_a_valid=1 and o_a_ready=1) happens at edge Ex.
Byte writes use PutPartialData (a_opcode=1). Full-word writes use PutFullData with a_size=2 and a_mask=1111.
INTR_TEST is only exercised with INTR_ENABLE=1 on the forced bits. This avoids the INTR_STATE-while-disabled case that D-004 leaves open.
'While rst_ni = 0' (D-016) is read as including the first clock edge after an asynchronous assertion, before the next rising edge (CHK-008, CHK-030).
From an accepted request with i_a_intg_flip=1 until reset, the shadow-model assertions (CHK-013, CHK-004, CHK-006, CHK-007) are disabled, as D-017 requires.

Every test except CHK-031 and CHK-032 runs in all four run-set configurations (GpioAsyncOn, GpioAsHwStrapsEn) = (1,1), (0,1), (1,0) and (0,0). CHK-031 runs only where GpioAsHwStrapsEn=1, and CHK-032 only where GpioAsHwStrapsEn=0.

decisions.question: Is the filter delay exactly 16 module clock cycles when the pin is an output, and does the input register reflect output changes only after that delay? Also, is the stable-input window restarted on any glitch?
decisions.answer: Not defined by the documents. D-007 applies: the exact count and whether a glitch restarts it are not checked; tests hold a new filtered value either at most 12 cycles (must not appear) or at least 24 cycles (must appear within 24 cycles). There is no pad model (INT-IO-002, D-021): DATA_IN follows i_gpio only, so output-to-input delay is not a case here.

decisions.question: Does INTR_STATE only show an interrupt when both INTR_ENABLE and an INTR_CTRL_EN bit are set, or does INTR_ENABLE only gate the output interrupt?
decisions.answer: The documents disagree and do not decide it. Per D-004 only the common part is checked: with INTR_ENABLE[i]=1 a configured event sets INTR_STATE[i]; with INTR_ENABLE[i]=0 o_intr_gpio[i] stays 0; INTR_STATE[i] after an event while INTR_ENABLE[i]=0 is not checked. Left open for the G4 reviewer.

decisions.question: What are the 'configurations of the run set'? They are not defined in the quotes.
decisions.answer: All four combinations are in the run set: base (GpioAsyncOn=1, GpioAsHwStrapsEn=1, two seeds), sync_off (0,1), straps_off (1,0) and min (0,0), one seed each.

decisions.question: MASKED_OE_* bits 31:16 are unchecked because the text says 0 and the field table says rw; should the designer settle which is correct?
decisions.answer: Not settled by the documents; D-002 stands (bits 31:16 of a MASKED_OE_* read are not checked; bits 15:0 are). Left open for the G4 reviewer.

decisions.question: Does 'no later than 4 cycles after the first rising edge' include or exclude that edge, and does it apply to the register read value or an internal flop? The latency bounds depend on this.
decisions.answer: Counting convention for D-018: let E0 be the first rising edge of clk_i at which i_gpio already has the new value. The bound is observed at the ports: a Get of DATA_IN accepted (a_valid and a_ready) at E0+4 or later returns the new value; likewise an INTR_STATE read accepted at E0+8 or later (filter off) shows the event, and o_intr_gpio follows D-018. Internal flops are never observed.

decisions.question: Can a status-type interrupt's INTR_STATE bit be read-only and follow the input directly, and does INTR_TEST still apply to it? The quote doesn't say.
decisions.answer: Out of scope: all gpio interrupts are event type (Hardware Interfaces, Interrupts table). Status-type interrupt rules are not verified for this design.

decisions.question: How long may a protocol lock-up persist before the pingfail alert must fire, i.e. what is the bound on 'eventually'?
decisions.answer: Out of scope: the wrapper never issues ping requests (INT-CFG-003), so ping timeouts and pingfail are not checked.

decisions.question: When a sender-side encoding error is signalled by alert_p/n being set to the same value and toggling, is the toggling period specified?
decisions.answer: Not checked: the sender-side encoding error signalling is not observable at the ports except through o_alert_integ_fail, which a correct sender never sets (INT-ALERT-002, D-017); no toggle period is checked.
